featured_reviews.name: Juned Ansari
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tried a full South Indian feast and every dish had its own vibe! The ambiance was calm, simple, and very comforting — the kind of place where you can just sit back, enjoy good food, and relax 🤍

Benne Dosa – Crispy on the outside, soft inside, and loaded with that rich buttery flavour. Simple yet addictive.

Davangere Masala Dosa – Thick, soft, buttery, and paired with a perfectly spiced masala filling. A very different experience from a regular masala dosa.

Chaas – Super refreshing, light, and the perfect balance between all the rich flavours.

Mushroom Biryani – Aromatic, flavourful, and packed with masala in every bite without being overly spicy.

Mysore Pak – Soft, rich, and literally melts in the mouth with every bite.

Filter Coffee – Strong, creamy, and the perfect ending to a wholesome South Indian meal.

featured_reviews.review_text:

We tried different varieties here ... podi idli, benne dosa, Bangalore dosa, open dosa, curd rice, kolam rice, and ended the meal with their classic filter coffee ☕🤎

The benne dosa had that perfect buttery crispness, the podi idlis were flavourful and comforting, and the rice varieties added such a wholesome touch to the meal. Overall, the food felt simple, satisfying, and very true to classic South Indian flavours.

Definitely one of those places you’d want to revisit for a comforting breakfast or a relaxed evening meal ✨

featured_reviews.name: Vaibhav Bhosale
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tanjore Tiffin Room, Versova – Authentic South Indian Delight!

Visited **Tanjore Tiffin Room, Versova** on Sunday with a group of 12, and the experience was fantastic!

The **Chicken Ghee Roast, Chicken Chintamani, and Pepper Chicken** were absolutely outstanding - rich, spicy, and packed with authentic South Indian flavors. 🍗🔥
We also loved the **Malabar Parotta, Appam, Idiyappam, and Dosa with Sambar** - soft, fresh, and perfect with the curries.

Veg dishes like **Jackfruit Cutlet and Jackfruit Biryani** were surprisingly delicious, and the **Chicken Biryani** was aromatic and generously portioned. The **Mango Mint Cooler** was a refreshing highlight after the spicy feast. 🥭❄️

If the main seating area is full, they have **additional seating inside WTF**, which is very convenient during peak hours.
They also offer a **tasting platter where the staff explains different curries and how they are used in cooking** - a brilliant concept for first-time visitors and food enthusiasts.

The restaurant is **just ~500 meters from Versova Metro Station**, making it very easy to reach. 🚇

For around **₹9.7K for 12 people (~₹800 per person)**, the quality, quantity, and taste were totally worth it.

**Highly recommended for authentic South Indian food and group outings! Will definitely visit again.**

featured_reviews.review_text:
This place is quite popular and is usually packed during both lunch and dinner, so making a reservation is a must. This was my second visit here, and of course we ordered their signature Railway Curry it never disappoints.

This time we also tried:
Mutton Cutlet
Mini Idlis
Veg Cutlet
Beef Roast with Lemon Rice
Egg Appams
Fried prawns

The mini idlis with ghee were absolutely delicious, and the beef roast was our next favourite.
Fried prawns was crispy and had a balanced taste.

I had high expectations from the mutton cutlet, but it didn’t quite live up to the hype. The lemon rice and egg appam were also slightly on the sweeter side, which didn’t go too well with our palate.

Their chutneys are amazing though definitely a highlight!

The staff is extremely warm and courteous, and the ambience is lovely. They even have a pet dog at the restaurant, but do be careful as it may suddenly run up or try to bite if you get too close.

Overall, a charming place with great service and some standout dishes, but a few items could be improved taste-wise.

We recently visited Banana Leaf, located at Ground Floor, Shubham CHS, Juhu Versova Link Road, Four Bungalows, Andheri West — and the experience was absolutely fantastic!

The ambience is beautifully inspired by South Indian themes, with both indoor and outdoor dining spaces. It’s the perfect spot for South Indian food lovers, and no surprise — it stays packed not only on weekends but even on weekdays.

They’ve introduced a brand-new Podi Festival menu, and it’s truly something special. Their new Kadipatta Podi, mixed with generous ghee and flavour, is a must-try!
Here’s what we ordered:
•	Tava Neer Dosa
•	South Canara Masala Dosa
•	Pacche Podi Rice
•	Ragi Semiya Upma
•	Mallige Set Green Podi Masala
•	Multigrain Onion Ada Dosa
•	Green Ghee Podi Mini Idli

Every dish was fresh, flavourful, and perfectly prepared.
We also tried their Filter Coffee, which was refreshing and completed the meal beautifully.

The service was top-notch — the staff, manager, and overall hospitality made the experience even better.

Overall: 10/10 experience.
This new Podi Festival menu is available across all Banana Leaf outlets in Mumbai, so visit your nearest one if you love authentic South Indian cuisine, especially their dosas and idlis.

featured_reviews.name: Dr Prasad Kamble
featured_reviews.review_text:
Banana Leaf is a great place for anyone who loves authentic vegetarian South Indian food. We tried a few of their delicacies—filter coffee, appam, and the Benne Podi Masala Dosa.
My absolute favorite was the Benne Podi Masala Dosa. It’s not like the traditional benne dosa that comes drenched in coconut oil—this version is neat, easy to eat, and definitely feels healthier. It’s served with white butter (makkhan), flavorful chutney, and sambar, which perfectly balance the dosa.
The filter coffee was comforting and well brewed, and the appam was soft and light. They have a wide range of South Indian delicacies on the menu, and there’s a lot more I’m looking forward to trying.
I’ll definitely keep updating my reviews as and when we visit again. For now, the Benne Podi Masala Dosa is completely on my mind and a must-try! 😋

First of all Salutations to Shri Pravin Shetty and many thanks to Shri Sudesh Rai as well. Each item was served hot, with the regular accompaniments, onion, lime, specially requested pickle, hot sambhar and coconut chutney.

Good quality tissues and an easily accessible washbasin make it convenient for clean up after a finger licking, palate tickling vegetarian meal. Being 100% vegetarian is the added advantage here. They accept all kinds of payments with no extra surcharge or service charges. The regulatory 5% GST is added to your bill amount.
A good hearty meal for five cost us less than 1500 including tips.
Even if you are very hungry and are good eaters, surely you won't spend more than 400-450 per person at this absolutely genuine vegetarian restaurant catering mostly to the College and school kids, especially during day time and the locals living in Andheri West, especially in the evenings.
Valet parking is available.

featured_reviews.review_text: Wow, what an experience! I went for brunch on a Friday with a friend. Yes, there was a queue, but we got a table in about 5 minutes of being in it. I’m a huge fan of podi, and wow, Namah did not disappoint. I ordered the ghee podi thatte idli and the benne masala dosa. The serving was good, and the dosa was SO NICE. My friend, who can’t even finish 3 bites of anything, ate that by herself! I also got the iced filter coffee, and OH, it was so balanced; it truly blew my mind. I ran into the founder, who I said hi to and congratulated her on the response she has gotten. It’s a very warm place. My personal opinion is that it’s okay to wait a bit to get inside a place, but it’s definitely worth it to experience it. Kudos to the Namah team for being thoughtful enough to open BIG from the start. We don’t really see that around much, I know.

featured_reviews.name: TravelWithDev04
featured_reviews.review_text:
Not worth the wait and hype

❌Overall Experience: 1.5/5
We visited Namah on our friend's birthday, I saw the reviews on instagram and everyone was talking about it, so we decided to give it a try. And we were disappointed by the food. It's a really beautiful place (architecture wise only), near Kokilaben Hospital, and you can go here just to see the architecture, skip the food.
We were 8 of us, luckily we went early and got a table, The cafe does not allow reservations, so you might have to wait in a long queue even to get in. Even if you say you have friends sitting inside, then they have to come to the door to bring you inside. The table was not really comfortable for 8 people. And some people have to stand and eat.
❌Food: 2/5
We ordered Benne dosa, it was served cold, thrice.
Benne podi dosa  was served hot, and it was ok.
I ordered butter milk and it was good.
People liked cold coffee.
A friend who ordered hot coffee did not like it.
Tamarind rice was served cold, had no taste at all, and in fact had a bit of bitter taste.
Curd rice was decent.
Bisi bele bhaat was ok ok.
❌Service: 2/5 Service was pretty average, as you have to stand in a queue in front of the automated touch screen ordering. (One of the kiosks was not working when we went there). Also the place is huge, so they call out your order number, but then most of the times you will not really hear it (could be one of the reasons why our food was always cold). The place feels overly crowded like a railway station.
✅Ambiance: 4/5 Architect has done a great job, and deserves an award to create a beautiful place at such a noisy road. This is the only thing you should go for. Though the wash basin is outside the facility. So in case you like washing hands before eating, then wash them before getting in the queue.
❌Value: We ended up spending about 300 per head, which was a decent amount, but not at all worth going again. If you have to stand and wait here, then go to any other south indian restaurant.

featured_reviews.review_text: Great place to have South Indian food. Quality of the food is very good. We had benne dosa, curd rice, medu wada and dessert. Everything was top notch. But yes you need to be there early. Otherwise be ready for the waiting time of 15-20 minutes during rush hours.

featured_reviews.name: gibran noorani
featured_reviews.review_text: We came with great expectations, especially after being hardcore fans of Benne and KTR, but unfortunately Namah was, in one word… underwhelming. The dosas are small but tasty, the podi though was slightly sweet, which i liked. Even the goli bhajiya were good but served slightly cold. The iced bournvita was excellent. But then the flipside was the Thatte Idli. The idli was too tough to eat. When I asked one of the servers about it… he said Thatte idli is supposed to be tough. I’m not a food expert but i have studied in Bangalore so I can assure Thatte Idli has to be soft. Then another server, heard this and immedialy got me another Idli. That was better but still not up to the mark. While introspecting we realised the AC vents in the room were very chilly and the servers were calling out our order numbers rather than putting up a board. Hence, a slight delay in  hearing can lead to your food turning cold.  So my biggest suggestion to control the AC temperature, and please improve your Idli. Overall, it’s a food you can try once but they need to buckle up better since they have a huge competition around them. Do check out their  exterior area which is a selfie point.

featured_reviews.name: Swapnil Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text: A masterclass in texture and spice, the Chole Samosa Chaat here is a sensory riot where the shattered, golden crunch of the samosa is beautifully surrendered to a deep, tangy chickpea curry, all elevated by a cooling drizzle of yogurt and the electric snap of fresh chutneys. To recreate this at home, simmer boiled chickpeas in a masala of onions, ginger-garlic, and amchoor, then ladle it over crushed hot samosas and finish with a snowfall of fine sev and chopped onions. In a sophisticated contrast, the Rava Dosa arrives as a shatteringly crisp, lacy veil of gold; its secret lies in a buttermilk-thin batter of semolina, rice flour, and cumin poured from a height onto a screaming-hot griddle until it develops its signature "Swiss-cheese" holes. Whether you’re diving into the indulgent, street-style chaos of the chaat or the ethereal, buttery crispness of the dosa, this is a dual-course experience that perfectly celebrates the diverse landscape of Indian soul food.

featured_reviews.name: Ankeeta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointing Experience – Food Safety Ignored & Unprofessional Behaviour
This was my first and last experience with this restaurant, and unfortunately, it has been deeply disturbing—not just because of the food issue but because of how the staff and social media team handled it.
I ordered Davanagere Benne Masala Dosa from the Malad West outlet and found hard, crystal/plastic-like foreign particles inside the food while eating. This is a serious food safety and hygiene violation, not a minor complaint.
When I contacted the restaurant, one of the staff members assured me that they would help and specifically guided me to approach Zomato and also email them, stating that this was the correct process. I followed their instructions exactly. However, Zomato outright refused to help or issue a refund, despite clear photographic evidence.
What is truly shocking is what followed next.
When I went back to the restaurant team and their social media handles for support, instead of standing by their words or taking responsibility, they completely changed their attitude.
My comments explaining the issue were deleted from their social media pages
Messages were left unanswered
There was no follow-up, no accountability, and no resolution
This behaviour feels like a deliberate attempt to silence genuine complaints rather than address a serious concern. Saying “we are here to help” and then deleting comments and ignoring the customer is highly unprofessional, unethical, and misleading.
If this is how a restaurant reacts to a food contamination issue, it raises serious questions about their internal standards and customer ethics. Customers are not asking for favours—we are asking for basic food safety and honest accountability.
I am extremely disappointed with the staff’s behaviour and the way the social media team handled this matter. This review is being posted so other customers are aware of how genuine issues are treated once money has already been taken.
Food quality, customer trust, and transparency clearly need urgent attention here.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Vishu at Kamat Legacy, Malad felt like a warm slice of Kerala right in the heart of Mumbai. Their Vishu Sadya Mango celebration wasn’t just a meal—it was a beautifully curated experience that brought tradition to life on a banana leaf. Every element, from the neatly arranged dishes to the authentic flavors, reflected attention to detail and respect for the festival.
The highlight, of course, was the mango-infused twist to the classic sadya. From the refreshing mango pachadi to the subtly sweet notes in the curries, each bite struck a perfect balance between nostalgia and innovation. The rice paired effortlessly with the rich sambar and avial, while the crispy papadam added that much-needed crunch. And ending the meal with a luscious mango payasam was nothing short of indulgent.
The ambiance complemented the experience—simple, clean, and rooted in South Indian culture—allowing the food to truly shine. The staff was courteous and ensured everything was served fresh and on time, enhancing the overall dining experience.
If you’re looking to celebrate Vishu in an authentic yet slightly contemporary way, this mango sadya at Kamat Legacy, Malad is definitely worth experiencing.

featured_reviews.name: ADITYA JAISWAL
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Kamats Legacy Malad for their Pongal Food Festival and absolutely loved it! Authentic South Indian flavours, beautifully served on a banana leaf with amazing variety. Unlimited feast, great quality, and a truly festive experience, Highly recommended!😍

featured_reviews.name: Gayatri
featured_reviews.review_text: Kamats Legacy truly lives up to its name with authentic South Indian taste and comforting flavours, all served the traditional way on a banana leaf. We tried the Murugappa Dosa and Benne Dosa both perfectly cooked with that rich, ghee-forward aroma. The Vithal Wada was crunchy and satisfying, while the Appam with Malabar Stew stood out for its light texture and beautifully balanced coconut flavours. The Chettinad Potato Roast was spicy and robust, and the Banana Kappa added a rustic, homely touch to the meal. Ending on a classic note with Filter Kaapi and refreshing Kuluki made the experience even better. A must-visit for anyone craving truly authentic South Indian food. 🌿🥥

featured_reviews.name: Dhaval Panchal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kamats Legacy on Malad West Link Road offers a brilliant dining experience for lovers of authentic South Indian cuisine.
​The highlight is definitely the Unlimited Buffet at an incredible price point of ₹499. The variety is extensive, and they maintain great quality across all the traditional dishes. It’s an absolute bargain for the quantity and flavor profile they offer.
​Key Highlights:
​Food Quality: Truly authentic and fresh. The Benne Dosa is exceptional—perfectly textured and generously buttery. A definite 5-star dish!
​Beverage: The Buttermilk (Chhas) deserves a special mention; it's one of the most flavorful and refreshing I've ever had.
​Value: ₹499 for unlimited, high-quality South Indian food is unbeatable in this area.
​Ambiance/Service: The restaurant is clean, and the staff are prompt and polite in serving the buffet items.
​If you are near Link Road and looking for a fulfilling, high-value South Indian meal, Kamats Legacy is the place to go. Highly recommended

featured_reviews.name: Ayushi Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Kamat’s Legacy in Malad to celebrate a colleague's birthday, and it was a disaster from start to finish. Despite a reservation for 30 people, they only had room for 20, forcing our group to squeeze in. The hygiene was questionable with flies buzzing around the table.
The worst part: we found a piece of metal (looked like a pressure cooker whistle) in the birthday girl’s thali. This is a massive safety violation. While the manager apologized and the chef came out, the manager’s first instinct was to whisk the metal piece away to hide the evidence. Out of 35 thalis ordered, they only waived the cost of one as "compensation."
Slow service, poor hygiene, and dangerous food. As a group of teachers from Children’s Academy, we expected much better. Do not recommend.

featured_reviews.name: Kuldip Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
🌿 Banana Leaf – A Slice of South India in Malad 🌿

If you’re looking for authentic South Indian vegetarian cuisine, Banana Leaf is easily one of the best in Malad. This place celebrates the flavors of the South with a menu that spans specialties from Andhra, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka — bringing the diversity of Southern kitchens onto your plate.

The variety is impressive: from crisp dosas, fluffy idlis, crunchy vadas, and hearty uttapams to full traditional meals. The highlight for me was their Dakshin Bhojanam Thali — a wholesome spread of curries paired with appam or parotta, with a choice of bisi bele bhath or steamed rice. Each bite was a journey through authentic regional flavors.

We also tried the Rasam Vada, and I must say — the rasam was outstanding. Honestly, I’d visit again just for that comforting, tangy-soulful bowl.

The ambience is cozy and minimalistic, enhanced by soft South Indian instrumental music and staff dressed in traditional attire — little touches that complete the cultural vibe. The service is warm, cordial, and attentive, making the whole experience even better.

💡 Verdict: A must-visit if you’re craving South Indian food — wholesome, authentic, and full of flavor. 🍛✨

featured_reviews.name: The Lucky Guide
featured_reviews.review_text:
I was browsing through the nearby restaurants available to try something different and this place stood out by offering Tamilnadu cuisine, though after seeing a few photos on Google I understood that this is not the place I would want to sit and eat so I rather do a take out.

I arrive at the restaurant within a 7-8 minute walk, it is located at the end if Gautam Buddh road after 2-3 shops towards the left in a small lane that leads towards link road.

There were 2 tables that were occupied, I ask the guy at the counter for a menu and browsed to notice Indian cuisine, a few Tamilnadu cuisines and Chinese cuisine, since I am still trying to find a restaurant that serves the right biryani I thought let's try the biryani out here as it said Tamilnadu style. Additionally I ordered a chicken 65 again Tamilnadu style.

Whilst waiting for the order, I asked if they had a take away menu to which he replied that the prices on that menu are old as they have now increased the prices on the new menu however all items are available and they do home delivery by charging what Dunzo charges them, which sounded pretty acceptable, in the mean time I observed the restaurant, it's a small decent place, looked clean from where I was waiting, now keep in mind this place is good for bachelor's only, I definitely do not recommend girls, women or families visiting.

The order was picked up within 10 minutes coz they weren't busy and I walk back home.

Let's talk about the food. I ate similar biryani when I was in Hyderabad, they don't serve a biryani masala like how the other typical one's are available out there, it was biryani flavored rice with one big piece of chicken leg, egg curry, onion raita, and a pappad.

The chicken 65 was masala coated red color deep fried chicken, Ike a dry snack, more like and South Indian boneless chicken lollipop.

The biryani rice was under cooked, could have been cooked for maybe 3-4 minutes more or maybe kept on dum to be perfectly cooked, the taste was definitely tamilian and it made me get the feeling of being in South India. I didn't get to taste the egg curry coz the biryani was so much that I couldn't eat anything more, I loved the onion raita and the big sized pappad. Overall I was more than jus satisfied with what was served.

To beat it all the biryani costed 140/- & the chicken 65 costed 100/-, believe me when I tell you this place lived up to all expectations after paying so less, and I must say they are doing a fabulous job catering to all those people who want to eat some good food & yet pocket friendly.

So all you people out there who are looking for a pocket friendly restaurant, you people must try this place coz I say it's more than worthit for the price you pay.
